:::{#exm-indset-in-np}
#### Independent set is in NP

Let $x$ be an input to [INDSET](#def-indset),
with a graph of $m$ vertices.
Its adjacency matrix has $m^2 \ge m$ entries, so $m \le |x|$.
Take $q(n) = n$ in @def-class-np,
so a certificate $u$ has $|x|$ binary digits.
Its first $m$ digits mark the vertices of a proposed independent set,
and the verifier ignores the rest.
The verifier checks that $k$ of those $m$ digits are $1$
and that no two marked vertices are adjacent.
That takes $O(m^2)$ lookups in the adjacency matrix,
which is polynomial in $|x|$.
$G$ has an independent set of $k$ vertices exactly when some such $u$ passes,
so INDSET is in NP (@def-class-np).
No polynomial-time algorithm that decides INDSET is known.
@arora2009computational [section 2.1] use the same example.

:::
